terms.p: An address with no guarantees attached: it may be null, may point at freed memory, and nothing tracks what else points at the same place.
The property that no possible use of a safe API can cause undefined behaviour; an API that can be broken by an ordinary caller is unsound.
A safe interface built over unsafe operations, where the wrapper itself checks whatever the compiler could not.
A comment above an unsafe block stating which precondition it relies on and why that precondition holds at that point.
The record of which allocation and which permission a pointer was derived from, which is part of whether using it is legal even when the address is right.
An interpreter that runs Rust at the intermediate-representation level and reports undefined behaviour that ordinary testing cannot see.
An attribute fixing how a type is laid out in memory, needed whenever another language has to agree about where the fields are.
Calling code written in another language, which is always unsafe because the compiler cannot see what that code does.
A type whose fields share one piece of storage, so reading a field asserts it is the field that was last written.
A mutable global variable with no synchronisation, so any two threads touching it are a data race and therefore undefined behaviour.
Reading one type's bytes as another type, which is undefined behaviour unless every possible bit pattern is valid for the target.
A trait whose correctness other code relies on for safety, so writing an impl requires the unsafe keyword and a stated justification.
